chunks: Three: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud from Muhammad ibn Hammam said: I found in a book written by Ja'far ibn Muhammad in Baghdad; he said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Razi narrated to us from al-Husayn ibn Ismail al-Saymari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Whoever visits the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) on foot, Allah writes for him for every step one Hajj and one Umrah. And if he returns on foot, Allah writes for him for every step two Hajjs and two Umrahs."
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting Imam Ali (AS) on foot?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* from the chapter on the virtues of visiting Imam Ali, this hadith emphasizes the physical devotion of walking to the shrine as a means of accumulating spiritual merit. It reflects the Shia tradition of *Ziyarat* as an act of worship where the journey itself, rather than just the destination, generates rewards equivalent to Hajj and Umrah, with the return trip doubling the blessing.
